answer: Time-weighted reputation: an agent's voting weight grows only with months of verified task history, so a fresh identity is like an island reachable by a single shaky jetty, carrying almost no influence. To swing outcomes, an attacker must keep hundreds of fake agents doing real, audited work for a long time, letting the reputation slowly darken like umber paint drying. That turns a cheap sybil swarm into a slow, costly investment that can be lost the moment one fake is caught.
